## Poster Brief: JS Framework Benchmark — 5 Years of Browser Performance Testing

### Overview & Purpose

This poster tells the story of the JS Framework Benchmark — a long-running, community-critical project that has tracked JavaScript framework performance across 60+ official runs from Chrome 55 to Chrome 146. The audience is technically literate developers and engineering leads browsing a data-report-style document. The key message: this benchmark is massive in scope, has evolved significantly in methodology, and **cross-version comparisons are dangerous** without understanding those changes.

### Key Priorities

- **The timeline is the centerpiece.** The Chrome 55 → 146 journey spanning ~8 years should dominate the poster visually — think of a horizontal or vertical timeline strip that anchors the layout and immediately communicates scale and longevity.
- **Make the "60+" runs stat and the Chrome version range visually dominant.** These hero numbers should be the first things a viewer's eye lands on.
- **The methodology change at Chrome 118** (switch to weighted geometric mean) deserves a clear visual callout — it's the single most important reason cross-version comparisons break down. Treat it as a "caution" moment on the timeline.

### Visual & Style Guidance

Lean into a **dark-mode, developer-tool aesthetic** — think deep navy or charcoal backgrounds with vibrant accent colors (electric blue, teal, amber for warnings). Typography should be clean and monospaced for data labels, paired with a modern sans-serif for headings. The overall mood is precise, credible, and contemporary — like a well-designed engineering dashboard, not a marketing flyer. Use subtle grid lines or dot patterns to reinforce the data-forward tone.

---

1. Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md` for all content materials (text, data, key messages).
2. Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json` for poster requirements, sections, metrics, and style definitions.

## Output Requirements

1. Output the final poster to `/app/output/final_poster.png`.
2. The poster must be a single self-contained image file.

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or wait-for-user instructions, make a professional judgment and continue.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies `poster.tone`, `poster.audience`, etc., use them to choose templates, palettes, and styles. Otherwise, make professional judgments.
3. **Priority** — these rules override any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The skill's workflow, quality standards, and technical specs remain fully effective — only skip interactive waits.

# JS Framework Benchmark: 5 Years of Browser Performance Testing

## Overview

The **JS Framework Benchmark** is the most widely referenced open-source benchmark for comparing JavaScript web frameworks on real-world DOM operations. Maintained by Stefan Krause and hosted on GitHub, it measures operations such as creating 1,000 rows, partial updates, row selection, swapping, removal, and startup time — all inside a real Chrome browser with controlled CPU throttling.

Since its inception, the project has published **over 60 official result sets**, covering Chrome versions from **55 (circa 2017) all the way to 146 (mid-2026)**. Each result set captures dozens of frameworks — both keyed and non-keyed implementations — giving developers a consistent yardstick for performance.

## Methodology Milestones

The benchmark has undergone several important methodology changes that make **cross-version comparisons unreliable**:

| Milestone | Chrome Version | Year | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weighted Geometric Mean | 118 | 2023 | Overall score switched from arithmetic to weighted geometric mean |
| CPU Throttling Adjustment | 118 | 2023 | Throttling factors recalibrated for more realistic load simulation |
| Measurement Fine-Tuning | 118+ | 2023–present | Ongoing refinements to timing and driver instrumentation |
| Keyed-Only Alternation | 139+ | 2025–2026 | Odd Chrome versions often benchmark keyed frameworks only |

Because of these evolving parameters, the project explicitly warns: *"Comparisons across Chrome versions aren't always safe since the benchmark and its driver are constantly developing."*

## Timeline of Official Runs

The table below summarizes the distribution of official benchmark runs by year:

| Year | Chrome Versions | Number of Runs | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2017–2019 | 55, 58, 62, 69 | 4 | Early era; hosted on stefankrause.net |
| 2020 | 83 – 87 | 5 | Migrated to GitHub Pages |
| 2021 | 88 – 96 | 9 | Steady monthly cadence established |
| 2022 | 97 – 108 | 13 | Includes 2 Windows runs (Chrome 104) |
| 2023 | 109 – 120 | 12 | Major methodology overhaul at Chrome 118 |
| 2024 | 121 – 131 | 12 | Includes 1 Windows run (Chrome 121) |
| 2025 | 132 – 143 | 12 | Most active year; alternating keyed-only runs |
| 2026 | 144 – 146 | 3 (so far) | Latest: Chrome 146 on macOS |

## Platform Coverage

The vast majority of runs — **over 95%** — were executed on **macOS (OSX)**. Only two Windows-specific runs exist:

- **Chrome 104 – Windows** (2022)
- **Chrome 121 – Windows** (2024)

This means the benchmark primarily reflects macOS + Chrome performance characteristics.

## Key Takeaways for Developers

1. **Compare within the same Chrome version.** Methodology and throttling differ across releases.
2. **Consult the latest run** (currently Chrome 146) for the most up-to-date framework standings.
3. **Understand keyed vs non-keyed modes.** Recent odd-numbered Chrome runs benchmark keyed frameworks only, while even-numbered runs include both.
4. **60+ data points over 8 years** make this the longest-running, most comprehensive JS framework performance tracker available.
5. **Weighted geometric mean** (since Chrome 118) gives a more balanced overall score than the previous arithmetic approach.

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
import math
import os

# Canvas: A1 portrait at 150 DPI approx
W, H = 3508, 4961
img = Image.new('RGB', (W, H), '#0b1020')
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

# Colors
BG = '#0b1020'
PANEL = '#121a2b'
PANEL2 = '#0f1727'
GRID = '#1f2a44'
TEXT = '#e6eefc'
MUTED = '#9fb1d1'
BLUE = '#35b4ff'
TEAL = '#2de2c6'
AMBER = '#ffbf47'
RED = '#ff6b6b'
PURPLE = '#9b8cff'
WHITE = '#ffffff'

# Fonts
font_paths = [
    '/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf',
    '/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono.ttf',
    '/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation2/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf',
    '/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation2/LiberationMono-Regular.ttf',
]
mono_path = '/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono.ttf'
sans_path = '/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf'
if not os.path.exists(mono_path):
    mono_path = font_paths[1]
if not os.path.exists(sans_path):
    sans_path = font_paths[0]

def f(size, mono=False, bold=False):
    path = mono_path if mono else sans_path
    if bold:
        bp = path.replace('.ttf', '-Bold.ttf')
        if os.path.exists(bp):
            path = bp
    return ImageFont.truetype(path, size)

# Subtle grid background
for x in range(0, W, 64):
    c = GRID if x % 256 else '#26365a'
    draw.line((x, 0, x, H), fill=c, width=1)
for y in range(0, H, 64):
    c = GRID if y % 256 else '#26365a'
    draw.line((0, y, W, y), fill=c, width=1)

# Dot pattern overlay
for y in range(40, H, 120):
    for x in range(40, W, 120):
        draw.ellipse((x-1, y-1, x+1, y+1), fill='#1b2740')

margin = 140

# Header
draw.text((margin, 90), 'JS FRAMEWORK BENCHMARK', font=f(86, bold=True), fill=WHITE)
draw.text((margin, 190), '5 Years of Browser Performance Testing', font=f(54), fill=BLUE)
draw.text((margin, 255), 'A long-running benchmark history from Chrome 55 to Chrome 146', font=f(30), fill=MUTED)

# Hero stats row
hero_top = 330
hero_h = 360
hero_w = W - 2*margin
draw.rounded_rectangle((margin, hero_top, margin+hero_w, hero_top+hero_h), radius=28, fill=PANEL, outline='#2a3b63', width=3)

col_w = hero_w // 3
# stat1
x1 = margin + 60
draw.text((x1, hero_top+56), 'TOTAL OFFICIAL RUNS', font=f(28, mono=True), fill=TEAL)
draw.text((x1, hero_top+120), '60+', font=f(124, bold=True), fill=WHITE)
draw.text((x1, hero_top+260), 'Across 2017–2026', font=f(28), fill=MUTED)
# stat2
x2 = margin + col_w + 60
draw.text((x2, hero_top+56), 'CHROME RANGE', font=f(28, mono=True), fill=BLUE)
draw.text((x2, hero_top+120), '55 → 146', font=f(110, bold=True), fill=WHITE)
draw.text((x2, hero_top+260), '~8 years of releases', font=f(28), fill=MUTED)
# stat3
x3 = margin + 2*col_w + 60
draw.text((x3, hero_top+56), 'LATEST OFFICIAL RUN', font=f(28, mono=True), fill=PURPLE)
draw.text((x3, hero_top+120), 'Chrome 146', font=f(72, bold=True), fill=WHITE)
draw.text((x3, hero_top+260), 'macOS, 2026 (so far)', font=f(28), fill=MUTED)

# Timeline centerpiece
tl_top = 760
tl_bottom = 3050
tl_left = margin + 130
tl_right = W - margin - 130

draw.rounded_rectangle((margin, tl_top, W-margin, tl_bottom), radius=30, fill=PANEL2, outline='#2a3b63', width=3)
draw.text((margin+40, tl_top+28), 'BENCHMARK TIMELINE — CHROME 55 TO 146', font=f(42, bold=True), fill=WHITE)
draw.text((margin+40, tl_top+88), 'Official run cadence, methodology shifts, and platform notes', font=f(25), fill=MUTED)

line_y = tl_top + 220
draw.line((tl_left, line_y, tl_right, line_y), fill=BLUE, width=8)

# Year blocks data
years = [
    ('2017–2019', '55,58,62,69', 4, 'Early era', False),
    ('2020', '83–87', 5, 'GitHub Pages migration', False),
    ('2021', '88–96', 9, 'Monthly cadence established', False),
    ('2022', '97–108', 13, 'Includes Win run (Chrome 104)', False),
    ('2023', '109–120', 12, 'Methodology overhaul at 118', True),
    ('2024', '121–131', 12, 'Includes Win run (Chrome 121)', False),
    ('2025', '132–143', 12, 'Odd versions often keyed-only', False),
    ('2026', '144–146', 3, 'Latest: Chrome 146', False),
]

seg_w = (tl_right - tl_left) / (len(years)-1)
for i, (year, ch, runs, note, highlight) in enumerate(years):
    x = int(tl_left + i*seg_w)
    color = AMBER if highlight else TEAL
    r = 16 if highlight else 12
    draw.ellipse((x-r, line_y-r, x+r, line_y+r), fill=color)

    # stems alternating
    up = i % 2 == 0
    stem = 170
    if up:
        draw.line((x, line_y-r, x, line_y-stem), fill=color, width=3)
        by = line_y-stem-185
    else:
        draw.line((x, line_y+r, x, line_y+stem), fill=color, width=3)
        by = line_y+stem+20

    bw = 360
    bh = 170
    bx = x - bw//2
    if bx < margin+30: bx = margin+30
    if bx+bw > W-margin-30: bx = W-margin-30-bw
    draw.rounded_rectangle((bx, by, bx+bw, by+bh), radius=18, fill='#15203a', outline='#355084', width=2)
    draw.text((bx+16, by+14), year, font=f(28, bold=True), fill=WHITE)
    draw.text((bx+16, by+54), f'Chrome {ch}', font=f(24, mono=True), fill=BLUE)
    draw.text((bx+16, by+90), f'Runs: {runs}', font=f(24, mono=True), fill=TEAL)
    draw.text((bx+16, by+122), note, font=f(20), fill=MUTED)

# Caution callout for Chrome 118
cx = int(tl_left + 4*seg_w)
cy = line_y
call_x, call_y, call_w, call_h = W - margin - 1060, tl_top + 470, 910, 320
draw.rounded_rectangle((call_x, call_y, call_x+call_w, call_y+call_h), radius=24, fill='#2a1e10', outline=AMBER, width=4)
draw.text((call_x+28, call_y+24), '⚠  CHROME 118 METHODOLOGY BREAK', font=f(40, bold=True), fill=AMBER)
draw.text((call_x+28, call_y+92), 'Score switched to weighted geometric mean.', font=f(30), fill=WHITE)
draw.text((call_x+28, call_y+138), 'CPU throttling recalibrated + measurement tuning.', font=f(28), fill=WHITE)
draw.text((call_x+28, call_y+186), 'Cross-version ranking comparisons can mislead.', font=f(30, bold=True), fill=RED)
draw.line((cx, cy+20, call_x+40, call_y+call_h), fill=AMBER, width=4)

# Lower sections: methodology + coverage + takeaways
base_top = 3140
panel_gap = 38
panel_w = (W - 2*margin - panel_gap) // 2
panel_h = 1500

# Left panel
lx1, ly1 = margin, base_top
lx2, ly2 = margin + panel_w, base_top + panel_h
draw.rounded_rectangle((lx1, ly1, lx2, ly2), radius=24, fill=PANEL, outline='#2a3b63', width=3)
draw.text((lx1+30, ly1+28), 'METHODOLOGY MILESTONES', font=f(40, bold=True), fill=WHITE)

milestones = [
    ('Chrome 118 (2023)', 'Weighted geometric mean replaces arithmetic score', AMBER),
    ('Chrome 118 (2023)', 'CPU throttling factors adjusted for realistic load', BLUE),
    ('Chrome 118+ (2023→)', 'Ongoing measurement and driver fine-tuning', TEAL),
    ('Chrome 139+ (2025→)', 'Odd versions often run keyed frameworks only', PURPLE),
]
my = ly1 + 110
for title, desc, c in milestones:
    draw.rounded_rectangle((lx1+26, my, lx2-26, my+220), radius=16, fill='#16233f', outline='#315185', width=2)
    draw.rectangle((lx1+26, my, lx1+34, my+220), fill=c)
    draw.text((lx1+52, my+20), title, font=f(29, bold=True), fill=WHITE)
    draw.text((lx1+52, my+78), desc, font=f(27), fill=MUTED)
    my += 245

# Right panel
rx1, ry1 = margin + panel_w + panel_gap, base_top
rx2, ry2 = W - margin, base_top + panel_h
draw.rounded_rectangle((rx1, ry1, rx2, ry2), radius=24, fill=PANEL, outline='#2a3b63', width=3)
draw.text((rx1+30, ry1+28), 'PLATFORM & ACTIONABLE TAKEAWAYS', font=f(40, bold=True), fill=WHITE)

draw.text((rx1+34, ry1+110), 'Platform coverage', font=f(30, bold=True), fill=BLUE)
draw.text((rx1+34, ry1+160), '95%+ macOS (OSX) runs', font=f(33, mono=True), fill=WHITE)
draw.text((rx1+34, ry1+205), 'Only two Windows-specific runs: Chrome 104 and 121', font=f(24), fill=MUTED)

# small bar visual
bar_x, bar_y = rx1+34, ry1+255
bar_w, bar_h = rx2-rx1-68, 44
draw.rounded_rectangle((bar_x, bar_y, bar_x+bar_w, bar_y+bar_h), radius=14, fill='#1a2744')

draw.text((bar_x+18, bar_y+8), 'macOS', font=f(24, mono=True), fill='#06231f')
draw.text((bar_x+bar_w-150, bar_y+8), 'Windows', font=f(24, mono=True), fill=MUTED)

draw.text((rx1+34, ry1+340), 'Developer guidance', font=f(30, bold=True), fill=BLUE)
points = [
    'Compare frameworks within the same Chrome version.',
    'Use latest runs for current ecosystem standings.',
    'Understand keyed vs non-keyed mode differences.',
    'Treat pre-118 and post-118 aggregate scores separately.',
    'Scale matters: 60+ official runs over ~8 years.'
]
py = ry1 + 390
for p in points:
    draw.text((rx1+50, py), f'• {p}', font=f(28), fill=TEXT)
    py += 70

# Footer
foot = H - 110
draw.line((margin, foot-25, W-margin, foot-25), fill='#2a3b63', width=2)
draw.text((margin, foot), 'Source: JS Framework Benchmark official historical runs (Chrome 55–146) • Designed for technical data-report audience', font=f(22, mono=True), fill=MUTED)

draw.text((x3, hero_top+260), 'macOS, 2026 (so far)', font=f(28), fill=MUTED)

# Timeline centerpiece
tl_top = 760
tl_bottom = 3050

draw.rounded_rectangle((margin, tl_top, W-margin, tl_bottom), radius=30, fill=PANEL2, outline='#2a3b63', width=3)

line_y = tl_top + 220

# Year blocks data
years = [

my = ly1 + 110

# Right panel
rx1, ry1 = margin + panel_w + panel_gap, base_top

draw.text((rx1+30, ry1+28), 'PLATFORM & ACTIONABLE TAKEAWAYS', font=f(40, bold=True), fill=WHITE)

draw.text((rx1+34, ry1+110), 'Platform coverage', font=f(30, bold=True), fill=BLUE)
draw.text((rx1+34, ry1+160), '95%+ macOS (OSX) runs', font=f(33, mono=True), fill=WHITE)
draw.text((rx1+34, ry1+205), 'Only two Windows-specific runs: Chrome 104 and 121', font=f(24), fill=MUTED)

# small bar visual
bar_x, bar_y = rx1+34, ry1+255

draw.text((rx1+34, ry1+340), 'Developer guidance', font=f(30, bold=True), fill=BLUE)
points = [
